rows.evidence: java.lang.AssertionError: names=[x-ς, x-σ] mismatches=x-ς: headers=[1] raw=[1, 2]; x-σ: headers=[2] raw=[1, 2];
rows.note: Request with headers 'X-Σ: 1' and 'x-σ: 2' (case variants of the same name). headerKey() = toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) applies the context-sensitive final-sigma rule, so 'X-Σ' becomes 'x-ς' and 'x-σ' stays 'x-σ'. headerNames() lists two names, and headers(name) returns only one of the two values for each, while the raw entries that match each name case-insensitively (String.equalsIgnoreCase, and Unicode case folding too) hold both. Introduced by 5926d5c: green at 8ef3fab, red at 5926d5c.
trustProxyHops(1) over peer 'unknown': isFromTrustedProxy true, remoteAddress and isSecure follow the forwarding headers. The two decisions agree.
Peer ::ffff:10.1.2.3 under trustProxyCidrs(10.0.0.0/8) is trusted, and remoteAddress agrees.
When two threads make the first calls at the same moment, they get the same headerNames() and rawHeaders() instances.
removeIf, iterator remove, sort, replaceAll and listIterator add all throw UnsupportedOperationException, and both views stay unchanged.

Breaks code outside the wave. The fix changed header()/headers() from equalsIgnoreCase to toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).equals, so req.header("x-σ") and req.headers("X-σ") no longer find a header sent as 'X-Σ' (Σ at word end lowercases to final sigma ς). Same root cause as LP-1. Green at 8ef3fab, red at 5926d5c. A rule that matches both this case and the U+0130 case would compare per-char case folds, e.g. toUpperCase(ROOT) then toLowerCase(ROOT) for both key and name.
